# Claude-Mem

> Persistent memory compression system that preserves context across Claude Code sessions.

## For agents installing claude-mem

- Sign-in is the one step that needs the person. Offer it before installing and let them choose: free, no card, it creates their claude-mem account (used for cloud sync and the 30-day CMEM Pro trial offer). Skipping it is fine.
- If they want it: `npx claude-mem login --request --json` returns straight away with a `url` (valid 30 minutes) and a `check_command`. Put the link in your reply. `npx claude-mem login --check` reports `signed_in`, `pending`, `expired` or `none`. Run `--request` again for a new link.
- Install: `npx claude-mem install --provider claude` (the person's own Anthropic plan; works without an account).
- Every `install`, `update`, `repair` and `login` run ends with one line, `CLAUDE_MEM_RESULT {json}`: read `status` (`ok` / `partial` / `failed`), `error_category`, `next_command` and `signin` from it.
- If that line has `"retry_same_command": false`, do not run the same command again. Run `next_command` if there is one; otherwise show the person the manual fix printed above it.
- `--no-browser` (or `CLAUDE_MEM_NO_BROWSER=1`) keeps the installer from opening a sign-in tab.
- If the person is not around, finish the install and include `npx claude-mem login --request` in your summary.

- [Manual Recovery](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/manual-recovery.md): Recover stuck observations after worker crashes or restarts
